key_insight: Lift4D bridges the gap between direct 4D prediction and deformation-based reconstruction by using strong single-view 3D estimation as a unified starting point for recovering dynamic objects in the wild. This lets the method combine learned priors with video evidence more effectively than approaches that rely on only one of them.
problem_solved: The paper addresses monocular 4D reconstruction of dynamic, non-rigid objects from in-the-wild video, where limited 4D training data and weak temporal supervision make accurate shape, motion, and appearance recovery difficult.
method: Use single-view 3D estimation to produce a strong initial 3D representation from one frame or view.
Harmonize learned priors with observed video cues to refine geometry, appearance, and deformation over time.
Reconstruct a coherent 4D representation that can better handle non-rigid motion and real-world video conditions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Lift4D offers a practical route to better dynamic scene reconstruction when multi-view data is unavailable. It is especially relevant for AR/VR, robotics, digital humans, and vision systems that need robust 3D understanding from everyday videos.

paper_title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Yehonathan Litman, Xiaoxuan Ma, Manan Shah, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Kris Kitani
